titulo: Gustar and preferences: Gustar: what pleases whom

aula.objetivo: Talk about what you like and don't like with gustar and encantar, agree and disagree with «a mí también / tampoco / sí / no», give a simple opinion, ask «¿qué te gusta?», and talk about free time.

blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: in English we say «I like coffee» — I is the one doing the liking. In Spanish the logic runs the other way: it's as if the coffee pleases me. The thing that's liked is the subject of the verb, and the person who likes it is marked with a pronoun: «Me gusta el café» (literally, coffee pleases me). STEP 2: the pronouns are «me, te, le, nos, os, les»: me gusta (to me), te gusta (to you), le gusta (to him, her, usted), nos gusta (to us), os gusta (to you-all, Spain), les gusta (to them, ustedes). STEP 3: the verb agrees with the thing that's liked, not with the person who likes it: if it's one thing, «gusta»; if it's several, «gustan»: «Me gusta el cine» (I like the movies), «Me gustan los gatos» (I like cats). STEP 4: if what's liked is an action, the verb stays in the infinitive and «gustar» stays singular: «Me gusta cantar» (I like to sing), «Me gusta cantar y bailar» (I like to sing and dance). STEP 5: the article is required before the noun: «Me gusta el café», never «Me gusta café». STEP 6: to negate, «no» comes before the pronoun: «No me gusta el café». STEP 7: intensity goes after the verb: «Me gusta mucho» (I like it a lot), «Me gusta bastante» (I like it quite a bit), «No me gusta nada» (I don't like it at all). To say you love something, «Me encanta» (singular) and «Me encantan» (plural) are common. To say you hate it, «Odio» (regular, subject I) or «No soporto» (I can't stand). STEP 8: with people, «Me gusta Pablo» suggests romantic attraction. To say you like someone as a friend, say «Pablo me cae bien» (Pablo strikes me well / I get along with Pablo). For family and friends, use «Quiero mucho a mi abuela» (I love my grandmother dearly).
blocos.comparacao: The meaning of «to like» is the same as in English, but the sentence structure runs opposite directions. English «I like music» (subject: I) corresponds to Spanish «Me gusta la música» (subject: the music). The two most common wrong paths — treating «gustar» as if the liker were the subject («Yo gusto la música»), or inserting «de» as English «of» might suggest («Me gusta de música») — don't exist in Spanish: there's never a «de» after «gustar».

linhas.exemplo: [misto] Me gusta el cine. / Me gusta leer.
[misto] Me encanta bailar. / Me encantan las playas.

erros.motivo: The one who likes it is the pronoun «me»; the coffee is the subject.
The verb agrees with «los gatos»: plural.
The article is required in Spanish.
After «gustar» there's no «de»; the infinitive follows directly.
The negation goes before the pronoun.

blocos.enunciado: Say six sentences out loud about what you like and don't like: three with «me gusta» and three with «me gustan». Include one with «me encanta» and one with «no me gusta nada».
Tell a friend out loud what you're wearing and what color each item is. Then say which you prefer between «este» and «ese».
